rules: If the destination register for c.ldsp is x0, the instruction is reserved.
If c.sdsp uses x0 as the source register, the entire 64-bit operand is zero, and register x1 is not accessed.
c.ldsp computes its effective address by adding the zero-extended offset, scaled by 8, to the stack pointer, x2.
c.ld computes an effective address by adding the zero-extended offset, scaled by 8, to the base address in register rs1'.
c.sd computes an effective address by adding the zero-extended offset, scaled by 8, to the base address in register rs1'.
c.sdsp computes an effective address by adding the zero-extended offset, scaled by 8, to the stack pointer, x2.
An LD or SD instruction whose effective address is a multiple of 4 gives rise to two 4-byte memory operations.
Decomposed sequences resulting from a 4-byte-aligned LD or SD instruction are interruptible.
Exceptions may occur on subsequent operations resulting from decomposed LD or SD sequences, making the effects of previous operations within the same instruction visible.
